doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

chapter: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
title: Lakefront camps, Blind Gilbert, and Sharkey sharing jobs
summary: Rene recalls the camps at Milneburg and West End and the trains out to them, then Sharkey Bonano, who passed jobs to the Rena band and played like Rene's brother.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: You know, the white folks used to have them picking, I don't know, no, I don't think you're old enough to remember Millenburg, Camps. Hey, you're parked! No, I didn't remember Millenburg. Millenburg, West End, they used to have camps. And just about from here to that kitchen, that's just how for a camp, then. And boy, you're talking about, they used to have a Spanish fort, uh, stuff to that kitchen. That is how far the camp's been. And boy, you're talking about, you used to have a Spanish fourth call run out there. It had about two, three cars hooked onto it, you know. And boy, you're talking about bass drums and basses. All the things that be loaded. One camp, fellas blowing that one another. You remember a fella too, Blind Gilbert, you ever heard of him? Who? Blind Gilbert. Gilby, no. White fella. Blind. No, I don't think I did. I had right up with him because he played plenty of trumpets. Oh yeah, Gilbert played up some trumpets. Gilbert. You know what band we used to work close with? You know, Sharky. Yes, I heard that. I knew Sharky is
a good friend of your brother's. Yeah, that's right. We used to play all the jobs that he couldn't take.
He'd give it to us. That's how we worked together. He's still playing it, I think. Oh, sure. Yeah.
Nice trumpet. Did he play somewhat similar to your brother? Didn't he sort of copy your brother?

Yeah. Yeah. And you know who played? He played like my brother played trumpet. P-Fa. That's the way my brother played trumpet. Just like that. Play it like that. You ever notice he plays? He makes his rung and thing, but he never gets away from his melody. Never get away from it. It stays right there with the melody.
